subject: ventures/hands-free-language-coach
professional: a language teacher / CALL (computer-assisted language learning) practitioner who has shipped spaced-repetition speaking drills, who would first ask: does the grader reject a wrong sentence, is the review schedule actually spaced, and does the drill reward only real attempts?

evidence.correctness: Ran `node --test` in the venture dir: 13 pass, 0 fail. Recomputed independently in Python (own NFD normaliser and Levenshtein, not the author's code) five similarity scores; all matched drill.mjs to 4 decimals: 'yo entiendo' vs 'No entiendo' 0.9091 (lev 1), 'buenas dias' vs 'Buenos dias' 0.9091, 'Ich verstehe' vs 'Ich verstehe nicht' 0.6667 (lev 6), 'Je comprends pas' vs 'Je ne comprends pas' 0.8421 (lev 3), 'Sim entendi' vs 'Nao entendi' 0.7273. Streak arithmetic checked by hand across a month and year boundary (02-28, 03-01, 03-02 gives 1,2,3; 12-31, 01-01 gives 1,2). The arithmetic is right; the verdicts are not what a teacher wants: 'Yo entiendo' (I understand) and 'Lo entiendo' pass as 'No entiendo' (I don't understand) at 91%, and 'Je comprends pas' passes for 'Je ne comprends pas'. Recogniser transcripts of a meaning-inverting one-letter error are graded a pass and the phrase moves up a Leitner box. Reading-only is not the basis: I executed grade() on these. Score 2: computes what it says, but the pass threshold is a character ratio with no word-level or negation check.
evidence.completeness: Claimed and checked: 5 packs (es, fr, de, it, pt) of 12 phrases each exist and the pack-shape test passes; grading, repeat/skip/stop parsing in English and target language (tested, executed); Leitner boxes, XP (+10/+4/+1 verified in recordAnswer), daily streak, share text (executed, test passes); usage counting with DNT/GPC off switch (usage.test.mjs passes); skill/SKILL.md and gpt/instructions.md present (39 lines, read SKILL.md). index.html wiring (wake lock, listen timeout, fallback mode) read in full and consistent with the README; no stubs or TODOs found. Not exercised: real Web Speech API in a browser (no browser here), so end-to-end speech was not run. Roadmap items (PWA, iOS, leagues) are correctly labelled planned, not shipped. Score 3.
evidence.verification: `node --test`: 13/13 pass. Seeded mutation 1: streak rule `gap === 1` changed to `gap <= 2` (a missed day keeps the streak): 13/13 still pass, not caught (the test only has gaps of 0, 1 and 3 days). Seeded mutation 2: `PASS = 0.8` changed to `0.6` (accepts much poorer answers): 13/13 still pass, not caught, because the grade tests only use identical or wildly wrong strings. Both mutations reverted, `git status` clean on the venture. No test covers the 'close' band, the CLOSE constant, mastered threshold beyond one case, the index.html session loop, or the fallback mode. Two uncaught core-logic mutations of two tried: score 1.
evidence.craft: Read drill.mjs (220 lines), usage.mjs, both test files, index.html in full. drill.mjs is clean: pure functions, no DOM, immutable progress updates, input coerced in normalize, unknown pack throws. usage.mjs swallows storage errors by design and says why. Defects: (a) in the no-recognition fallback, every phrase is recorded as 'close' with no attempt checked (index.html ~line 188), so XP (+4) is awarded and boxes reset to 0 for merely listening; (b) streak is awarded if answered > 0, so a user who says 'stop' after one phrase gets a streak day though README says 'one finished session a day'; (c) `levenshtein` compares UTF-16 units, fine for these Latin packs but would split astral characters; (d) listen() has a fixed 8 s timeout and no handling for a denied microphone beyond treating it as an empty answer, so a user who denied the mic gets 'Let's try that again' loops then failures with no spoken explanation; (e) command 'para' in es and pt packs is also a real word, partly mitigated by the 3-word limit. Reasonable engineering, a few silent fallbacks: 3.
evidence.claims: Checked README, index.html, llms.txt, VENTURE.yaml. Backed: scoring is described honestly as 'whether a recogniser understood you, not a phonetic assessment' (matches grade()); privacy (nothing uploaded, Chrome may send audio to its speech service, events counted locally, DNT/GPC) is backed by usage.mjs and its tests; disclaimer text and driving-safety text present on page and README. Not backed or wrong: (1) README says 'missed twice: it comes back first next session'; code does that only via box 0, but 'close' after two tries also resets to 0 and a fallback-mode session credits every phrase, which the README does not disclose; (2) 'spaced review' / 'Spaced repetition' (JSON-LD, page) is an ordering by box, with no time interval: planSession never looks at dates, so phrases are not spaced in time, they recur every session until 8 or more have moved up; (3) 'one finished session a day keeps your streak' is not what the code does (any answered phrase); (4) llms.txt links to https://duncan-haywood.github.io/oss-monorepo/hands-free-language-coach/, the retired Pages host, while the README and VENTURE.yaml say https://marisstella.app/hands-free-language-coach/; the page itself links 'Free tools' to the old github.io host; (5) llms.txt carries the boilerplate 'not legal, tax, financial' sentence, irrelevant to a language app; (6) sitemap.xml has `<loc>./</loc>`, which is not a valid absolute URL, and `<link rel=canonical href="./">` is relative. Score 2.
evidence.fitness: Walked the job of a commuter practising Spanish: Start, coach says English then Spanish, listens, grades, repeats, moves on, saves progress, shares streak. That loop works as designed in code. But a learner with 12 phrases per language gets about 2 sessions of material before it is memorised and repeats; the pack lacks verbs, numbers, tenses, and has no pronunciation feedback, so the 'learn a language' job is only partly met. Wrong-meaning answers pass (see correctness). Without speech recognition (Firefox, many mobile browsers) it degrades to a listen-only mode that still gives XP and streaks. The assistant skill is the more useful deliverable: the protocol is sensible and voice-safe. Score 2: a usable phrasebook drill, not a course.
evidence.domain: Compared against standard SRS practice (Leitner with day-based intervals, SM-2 / FSRS) and CALL guidance on speech-recognition scoring (grade at word or concept level, flag omitted negations and content words, do not equate string similarity with intelligibility). Departures: no time-based scheduling at all; a single whole-string edit-distance threshold with 0.8 pass so short phrases (11 characters) tolerate 2 wrong characters, including a meaning-flipping one; no per-word diff to tell the learner which word was wrong (the skill file does ask the model to name the single most important fix, the browser does not). Phrase content I checked as a reader of the languages is idiomatic and correct (Quisiera un cafe, Ich haette gern einen Kaffee, Dov'e la stazione, Voce pode falar mais devagar). The 'Moves up a box' and commands design are sound basics; the scoring disclaimer is honest. Score 2.

defects.what: Grader passes meaning-inverting near-misses: 'Yo/Lo entiendo' scores 0.91 and passes for 'No entiendo'; 'Je comprends pas' passes for 'Je ne comprends pas'. Whole-string edit-distance threshold with no word-level check, so a dropped or altered negation is rewarded with +10 XP and a box promotion.

Tests do not catch core-logic changes: changing PASS from 0.8 to 0.6 and changing the streak rule to tolerate a missed day both leave 13/13 tests passing. The 'close' band, CLOSE constant and streak gap of 2 are untested.
Without speech recognition the session records every phrase as 'close' with no answer checked: +4 XP per phrase, box reset to 0, and a streak day, for listening only.
'Spaced review' is ordering by box only; no dates or intervals, so it is not spaced repetition as the page and JSON-LD describe it.
Streak is awarded after any single answered phrase, even if the user said stop, contradicting 'one finished session a day'.

llms.txt and the page's 'Free tools' link point to the retired github.io host instead of https://marisstella.app/hands-free-language-coach/; sitemap.xml has a relative <loc> and the canonical link is relative; llms.txt carries an irrelevant 'not legal, tax, financial' line.
Only 12 phrases per language and no microphone-denied handling, so a user who denies mic permission hears repeated retries instead of an explanation.

verdict: A tidy, honest, zero-cost prototype whose arithmetic is right (five similarity scores and the streak logic recomputed independently and matched) and whose privacy and scoring caveats are truthful, but it does not meet the bar. Its grader rewards meaning-inverting errors such as 'Yo entiendo' for 'No entiendo', its 'spaced review' has no time dimension, its listen-only mode awards XP and streaks for no attempt, and its tests are weak enough that two seeded core mutations (pass threshold 0.8 to 0.6, streak tolerating a missed day) both survived with 13/13 passing. It is finished against what it claims to ship (completeness 3) but verification (1), correctness (2) and claims (2) keep it below the bar. Real browser speech was not run in this audit.
